work.title: Thränen der Sünder bey dem Kreuze Ihres Erlösers. Ein Oratorium

history.p: The work was performed for the first time in 1746 during Lent by The Musical Society (Det musikalske Selskab) which had been founded the previous year. In addition to Scheibe, also the composer Carl August Thielo and the playwright, philosopher and professor at the university Ludvig Holberg who was also a close friend of Scheibe’s were among the Society’s most influential members. Already in 1742, Scheibe composed a Passion cantata (SchW B2:304) which had been performed in the royal church. Three years later the Society also performed Passion music and now – with Scheibe’s work – it became a tradition that the societies during the eighteenth century performed Passion oratorios or cantatas at Lent. Scheibe wrote both text and music to ‘Thränen der Sünder’, though the cantata is interspersed with various known and popular chorales and Lutheran hymns by Paul Gerhardt among others. On the only surviving copy of the text book of 1746, the names of singers have been added in pencil. The cantata was performed again the following year, and it is possible that an undated libretto is from that event. The cantata was later performed in 1754 – perhaps on two occasions – and the libretto was reviewed in Fortgesetzte Nachrichten (1758): 'The author has composed this musical oratorio solely as a contemplation on the death of Jesus, a kind of Passion cantata which, to a certain extent and in regards to edification, has an advantage over others. There are some turns of phrases in it which must remind the reader of the familiar place in the song "O Traurigkeit, o Herzeleid etc." [...] We know how such expressions may be defended; it is, however, without doubt much better if we exclude the very same.' The recitatives are not indicated in the Høpfner edition, which unfortunately does not contain a publication date, but are in the Lillie edition of 1754.

annot.p: 'Der Hr. Verfasser hat dieses musikalische Oratorium als bloße Betrachtungen über den Tod Jesu abgefasset, welche Art von Paßionscantaten in gewisser Maße und in Ansehen der Erbauung einen Vorzug vor andern hat. Es kommen manche Redensarten darinn vor, die den Leser an die bekannte Stelle in dem Liede O Traurigkeit, o Herzeleid &c erinnern müssen [...] Wir wissen zwar, wie sich dergleichen Ausdrücke vertheidigen lassen, es ist aber doch ohne allen Zweifel viel besser, wenn man sich derselben enthält.'

incipText.p: Das ist der grosse Tag
In JEsu Blut erfüllten Wunden
Es dient zu meinen Freuden
Erlöser! Da deine gemarterten Glieder ersterben
Für alle Sünde, die du je begangen
Doch ach! wie klein ist nicht die Zahl
Mit JEsus Blut erkauffte Seelen!
Wisset, daß ihr nicht mit vergänglichen Silber oder Gold erlöst seyd
Ein Lämmlein geht und trägt die Schuld der Welt
O! daß ich könnte Trähnen gnug vergiessen!
Heyland! ach, bey deinem Schmerze
Ja wohl, mein GOtt! dein Lieben
Bey diesem erstaunenden göttlichen Lieben
Ach grosser König, groß zu allen Zeiten!
Liebreicher Heyland, ja mir gehn die Schmerzen
Höllische Feinde, was wütet ihr noch?
O JEsu! wahrer Fürst des Lebens!
Wie werd ich denn so frölich seyn
Ihr aber, die ihr hier vor JEsu Augen stehet
So weinet, Sünder, weinet Blut!
Lasset uns mit Jesu sterben

physDesc.physMedium: In 8o; title page (sig. [)(1r]), text (sigs. [)(1v]–)(4v); in all 8 unnumbered pages. Source includes eighteenth-century additions in pencil that most likely are the names of the singers: 'Iversen' (Johannes Erasmus Iversen); 'Sk. d. [= Skolediscipel] Jens', possibly Jens Musted; 'Bager'; 'Mad. Stolle' (presumably Jacobine Stolle).
Unbound, but pages trimmed; paper of a soft inferior quality.

physDesc.physMedium: In 4o; title page (sig. [A1r]), epigraph by Martin Opitz (sig. [A1v]), text (sigs. A2r–B2v); in all 12 unnumbered pages.

In library binding, half-bound with brown marbled hard covers, red title label with gold lettering pasted on front board; binding includes several different librettos, and extra paper have been pasted on to the margins of pages of the present work so that all pages are of the same size; top edge trimmed.
